title: Best Pillows for Neck Pain UK
short: Memory foam, wool and adjustable pillows compared by sleep position, firmness and who they suit.
intro: The wrong pillow height is a common cause of morning neck and shoulder pain, and the right pillow depends heavily on whether you sleep on your side, back or front. This guide compares pillows tested by Mumsnet, including adjustable options that let you fine-tune the height yourself.

guide.q: What pillow height do I need for my sleep position?
guide.a: Side sleepers generally need a taller, firmer pillow to fill the gap between ear and shoulder and keep the spine level. Back sleepers usually need a medium loft, and front sleepers generally need the lowest, softest pillow, or sometimes none at all.

If you are unsure what height or firmness suits you, an adjustable pillow like the Emma Adapt or Simba Hybrid lets you add or remove filling until it feels right, which can save buying several pillows to find the correct one.

guide.q: How often should I replace a pillow?
guide.a: As a general guide, most pillows are recommended for replacement every one to two years, since fillings compress and lose support over time, and a flattened pillow is less able to keep your neck properly aligned.

Memory foam contours closely to the head and neck and often suits neck pain well, but can retain heat. Natural fillings like wool regulate temperature better and are often hypoallergenic, but usually need airing rather than a machine wash.
